title: Handling Validation Errors
learning_outcomes: Explain what handling validation errors contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: field-specific errors.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Form values arrive as untrusted strings and may be absent, malformed, or repeated. Normalize them, validate business rules on the server, preserve safe user input when showing errors, and escape values on output. In this lesson, focus on field-specific errors; then compare it with preserving safe form values. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use handling validation errors when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Form values arrive as untrusted strings and may be absent, malformed, or repeated. Normalize them, validate business rules on the server, preserve safe user input when showing errors, and escape values on output. For handling validation errors, begin with field-specific errors. Also distinguish preserving safe form values; clear feedback; multiple validation failures. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
